{"query":"link no telemetry collector gap versus link down, traffic shift reroute","results":[{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":4.755,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"},{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":4.692,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"}]}

{"query":"link discards degradation versus link down flapping","results":[{"runbook":"RB05_link_degradation","score":4.062,"text":"# RB05 Link degradation (loss or latency)

Fault type: link_degradation. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The link stays up, but its one-hop latency rises (link_latency_high) or it drops packets (link_discards).
- Services crossing the link breach latency or loss SLAs; services not crossing it are fine.
- Utilisation is often unchanged, because routing does not move traffic away from a degraded but up link.

Checks:
- Compare the link's latency and discards with the same window one day earlier.
- Find the element shared by the paths of the services with SLA alerts; a degraded link is usually on all of them.
- Small degradations may raise no alert: look at the telemetry of links on the shared paths even without alerts.

Action: raise with the transmission team; consider moving traffic off the link with a metric change.
"},{"runbook":"RB04_link_flapping","score":3.75,"text":"# RB04 Link flapping

Fault type: link_flapping. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface goes down and up repeatedly; several short link_status_down alerts on the same link, or intermittent gaps in its telemetry.
- Repeated short bursts of loss on services that cross the link as routing converges each time.
- Utilisation on the link drops and recovers repeatedly; neighbours show matching opposite swings.

Checks:
- Count down/up episodes on the link in the window: more than one short episode is the signature.
- Rule out a collector problem: intermittent gaps on many unrelated links at once are not flapping.

Action: dampen or shut the interface and reroute; check optics and physical layer.
"}]}

Fault type: routing_misconfig. Root: the link whose routing metric was changed.

Symptoms:
- Traffic moves suddenly at one step: utilisation drops on one link and rises on others (metric raised), or rises sharply on one link (metric lowered, pulling traffic onto it).
- No interface goes down. Service latency changes because paths changed.
- Unlike a drain, there is no matching entry in the change log.

Checks:
- Look for a step change in utilisation on one link with no outage and no logged change.
- If a link lost most of its traffic while staying up, and nothing is logged, the metric on that link is the likely root.

Action: compare the running routing metric with the intended configuration; roll back the change.
"},{"runbook":"RB03_node_down","score":4.405,"text":"# RB03 Router (PoP) down

Fault type: node_down. Root: a PoP (router).

- The router stops answering polls (pop_unreachable) when status polling exists.

- Services that start or end at the PoP become unreachable; services that transited it reroute.

Checks:
- Do all links of one PoP show the same outage at the same step? A single dark link is a link fault; all links of one router is the router.
